conventions: Hand-cleaned from archive.org OCR of SII Vol II (Hultzsch/Venkayya). Diacritics simplified to plain ASCII (Rajendra-Choladeva, kasu, karanju, manjadi, kunri, kalam, marakkal, viral, muram). Reconstructions in [brackets]. Scan gaps marked [illegible in scan]. Photo pairing is UNVERIFIED (Commons photos are not labeled by SII number).
corpus: South-Indian Inscriptions Vol II, Rajarajesvara Temple, Tanjavur (Hultzsch 1891-1895; Venkayya 1913). Public domain (pre-1929 ASI publication).

entries.intro: Nos. 9 to 19 are engraved continuously in two sections of seven and ten lines. No. 9 is dated in the 6th year of Ko-Parakesarivarman alias Rajendra-Choladeva and fixes the interest payable to the temple by villagers on money contributed by donors and the temple treasury: for the chief idol (para 2) and the images of Kratarjuniyadevar and Pichchadevar (paras 3-4). The former was set up by a minister also named in the large Leyden grant, the latter by Lokamahadevi, queen of Rajarajadeva.
translation: Hail! Prosperity! In the sixth year of Ko-Parakesarivarman alias the lord Sri-Rajendra-Choladeva, who rejoiced that Fortune had become constant and the goddesses of earth, victory and fame his queens, and who conquered Idaiturai-nadu, Vanavasi, Kollippakkai, Mannaikkadakkam, the crowns of Ilam, the Ila-mandalam, the Kerala king's treasures and many seagirt islands: there was engraved on stone the money deposited to interest by the guru Isanasiva-pandita; by minister Udayadivakaran Tillaiyaliyar alias Rajaraja-Mavenda-Velar of Kanchivayil; by the Valangai-parambadaigalilar; and out of the temple treasury; with the village that took the money.

The guru Isanasiva-pandita deposited 180 kasu at one-eighth kasu yearly interest per kasu, yielding 22.5 kasu for 56.25 karanju of camphor: 3 manjadi daily for the god's food (54 karanju a year) plus a quarter karanju on each of the 9 festival days.
The minister deposited 13 kasu for the food and needs of Kratarjuniyadevar, whom he had set up.
Adding 805 kasu from the sacred treasury and 252 kasu deposited by the Valangai troops attached to Pichchadevar (set up by queen Lokamahadevi), the total is 1250 kasu.

The assembly of Nedumanal alias Madanamanjari-chaturvedimangalam in Neymali-nadu of Arumolideva-valanadu received 1070 kasu from Chandesvaradeva and must measure 267 kalam, 1 tuni, 1 padakku of paddy yearly into the Tanjavur treasury with the Adavallan marakkal, at 3 kuruni per kasu.
The same villagers pay 22.5 kasu yearly on the remaining 180 kasu at one-eighth kasu per kasu.

entries.intro: Dated in the 10th year of Ko-Parakesarivarman alias Rajendra-Choladeva. Fixes interest payable by a village for the image of Kratarjunadevar and the images of Maha-Meru-Vitankar and his consort. The first was set up by the minister of No. 9, the second by king Rajarajadeva.
translation: Hail! Prosperity! In the tenth year of Rajendra-Choladeva, conqueror of Idaiturai-nadu to the seagirt islands, holder of Parasurama's gold crown from Sandimattivu and of 7.5 lakh Iratta-padi taken from Jayasimha at Muyangi: engraved is the village that took on interest from Chandesvaradeva money for Kratarjunadevar (set up by minister Udayadivakaran Tillaiyaliyar of Kanchivayil) and money deposited by the Sirudanattu Panimakkal for Maha-Meru-Vitankar (set up by Rajarajadeva) and his consort.

The assembly of Irumbudal alias Manukulachilamani-chaturvedimangalam, a brahmadeya in Avar-kurram of Nittavinoda-valanadu, received 600 kasu (94 for Kratarjunadevar, 506 for Maha-Meru-Vitankar and consort) and must measure 150 kalam of paddy yearly into the Tanjavur treasury with the Adavallan marakkal, at 3 kuruni per kasu.

entries.intro: Same date as No. 10. Records endowments to the last two images of No. 10 and to Kalyanasundarar and his consort, the former set up by Trailokyamahadevi, queen of Rajarajadeva.
translation: [In the tenth year of] Rajendra-Choladeva: the assembly of Arumorideva-chaturvedimangalam in Purangarambai-nadu of Arumorideva-valanadu received from Chandesvaradeva 294 kasu of the money deposited by the Niyayam Sirudanattu Panimakkal attached to Maha-Meru-Vitankar (set up by Rajarajadeva) and his consort. And of the money deposited by the Niyayam [Ve]langai[lar] attached to Kalyanasundarar (set up by queen Trailokyamahadevi) and his consort, the Keralantaka gate-keepers received 118 kasu, the Anukka gate-keepers 8, the Keralantaka chosen retinue 35, the Jananatha chosen retinue 5, the Singalantaka chosen retinue 1, and the Parivara guards [illegible in scan; list breaks off].

entries.intro: Same year as No. 10. Records endowments to an image whose name is lost (supplied from No. 13) and to Chandesvaradeva, set up by a person also named in the large Leyden grant.
translation: After the pasam harvest in the tenth year of Rajendra-Choladeva, the assembly of Palliyil in Nenmali-nadu of Arulmolideva-valanadu received from Chandesvaradeva 104 kasu: 31 from the Pandita-Sora-terinda-villigal of the Niyayam Perundanattu Valangai-velaikkara troops attached to the Sri-Rajarajesvara; 13 from the Nittavinoda-terinda-valangai-velaikkaran; and 60 from the Niyayam Uttama-Sora-terinda-andalagattalar attached to Chandesvaradeva, set up by Perundanam [name lost] alias Mummadi-Sora-Posan alias Uttama-Sora-Pallavaraiyan.
On these 104 kasu they pay 13 kasu yearly interest into the temple treasury, at one-eighth kasu per kasu.

entries.intro: On a pillar of the south enclosure. Describes copper images of Siva, his wife and their two sons, set up by an officer of Rajarajadeva before the 29th year of his reign.
translation: Hail! Prosperity! The following copper images, set up in the Sri-Rajarajesvara temple before the 29th year by Velan Adittan alias Parantaka-Pallavaraiyan, headman of [place lost] and Perundaram of Rajarajadeva, were engraved on stone after measuring with the temple cubit and weighing the jewels by the Dakshina-Meru-Vitankan stone.
One solid image of Siva, husband of Uma, four-armed, seated: 14.5 viral from seat to hair.
One solid image of his consort Umaparamesvari, seated: 11.5 viral from seat to hair.
One solid image of Subrahmanya, two-armed, standing: 5.5 viral from feet to hair.
One solid image of Ganapati, four-armed: [height] viral from feet to hair.
[illegible in scan: pedestal, one muram and a half in length, fifteen viral ...]

entries.intro: On two pillars of the west enclosure. Dated in the 3rd year of Rajendra-Choladeva; records a copper image set up by the temple manager known from 29th-year Rajaraja inscriptions. Quotes the Tiruttontar legend of Meypporunayanar as in the Periyapuranam: stabbed by an enemy disguised as a Saiva devotee, the dying king stops his door-keeper Tattan from revenge with 'he is one of us'.
translation: Hail! Prosperity! In the third year of Ko-Parakesarivarman alias Sri-Rajendra-Choladeva, the copper images which Adittan Suryan alias Tennavan Mavenda-Velan, headman of Poygai-nadu and manager of the Sri-Rajarajesvara temple, had caused to be made were engraved on stone after measuring with the temple cubit and weighing the jewels by the Dakshina-Meru-Vitankan stone.
One solid Miladudaiyar, who said: 'Oh Tattan! he is one of us; see!' Two-armed, 20 viral from feet to hair.

entries.intro: On a niche (same as No. 41) and pillar of the west enclosure. Before the 29th year of Rajarajadeva, queen Cholamahadevi set up copper images of Siva Adavallar and his consort and gave ornaments to both.
translation: Hail! Prosperity! The copper images set up by Seramahadeviyar, consort of Rajarajadeva, before the 29th year were engraved on stone after measuring with the temple cubit, weighing jewels by the Dakshina-Meru-Vitankan stone and gold by the Adavallan stone.
Adavallar: four arms, Ganga on the braided hair, nine braids, seven garlands, with Musalagan underfoot; 7/8 muram feet to hair.
Jewelled lotus beneath: 3 viral high. Pedestal: 5 viral high, half a muram long, 10 viral broad. Solid aureola: 3 muram 2 viral round.
Consort Umaparamesvari: 17 viral 2 seradu feet to hair, on a jewelled 2 viral 2 terai lotus and pedestal; aureola 2 muram 14.5 viral round.
To Adavallar: a bead string of 6.5 karanju 1 manjadi of gold.

To the consort: a spiral of ruby on gold string (1.5 karanju, 2 manjadi, 1 kunri with lac; 4 kasu) set with diamonds, rubies and emerald; a 3-string ornament (3.75 karanju, 4 manjadi; 8 kasu) strung with 87 pearls of seven kinds, 6 corals and gold pins; a tali bead string (1.75 karanju, 2 manjadi, 1 kunri of gold).

entries.intro: On the base of the west enclosure. Date and donor partly lost, doubtless as in Nos. 40-41. Records copper images of Ksetrapaladeva and Bhairava plus a group of three humans: Siruttonda-Nambi, wife Tiruvenkattu-Nangai and son Siraladevar, whom the parents killed and served to Siva-as-Bhairava per the Periyapuranam. Proof of the legend's antiquity; Siruttondan already appears in Tirujnanasambandar's Devaram.
translation: Copper images of gods and men, set up before the 3rd year by [..] Mavenda-Velan, engraved after measuring with the temple cubit, weighing gold by the Adavallan stone and jewels by the Dakshina-Meru-Vitankan stone.
Ksetrapaladeva: eight arms, 7/8 muram; pedestal 9 viral square; bead string of 1/4 karanju gold; front-plate of 7 manjadi; ear-plates of 3 manjadi.

Sri-Bhairava dancing: two arms, 18 viral; pedestal 9 by 8 viral; bead string of 4 manjadi; a string (1/2 karanju, 4 manjadi, 1 kunri; 1/4 kasu) with 33 pearls; a string (8 manjadi; 1/4 kasu) with 37 pearls.
Siruttonda-Nambi: 17 viral; bead string (3 manjadi, 1 kunri); rudraksha collar (1/2 karanju, 1 manjadi of gold).
Tiruvenkattu-Nangai: 15 viral; neck-ring (9 manjadi, 1 kunri) with tali.
Siraladevar: 12 viral; front-plate (4 manjadi); ear-plates (1 manjadi, 1 kunri); neck-ring and spear (1/2 karanju, 4 manjadi, 1 kunri). Group pedestal with lotus: 23 viral long, 7 broad, 8 high.
